evidence.quote: A preliminary bimodal picture of DSFGs is appearing, where lensed sources are indicative of typically central dusty star-bursts, found in other surveys to be rotationally stable, while the weakly- or unlensed HyLIRGs could represent turbulent massive star-forming events driven by unstable galaxy kinematics and clumpy gas flows.

claims.hypothesis: Sharing calibration across clustered sources (<10 deg) and optimizing frequency tunings to known spectroscopic redshifts enables a rapid, high-efficiency multi-band ALMA line survey.
claims.experiment: Observed 16 Herschel fields in 2-minute snapshots across ALMA Bands 3 through 8 (6.5 hours total) using single optimized frequency tunings per band.
claims.result: Targeted 94 spectral lines and detected 66 lines (54 emission, 12 absorption) across 17 galaxies, achieving a 70% detection rate and 1 detected line every 6 minutes.
claims.finding: The ANGELS method doubles to increases by an order of magnitude the line detection efficiency compared to traditional overhead-limited surveys.

evidence.quote: In total, 94 spectral lines were targeted across 28 different line transitions. On average, each source is observed in five transitions, with HerBS-41A being targeted in as many as 12 lines. 66 lines were detected, resulting in a detection ratio of 70%.

As such, clustering is an important tool for future spectral surveys, and the ANGELS method demonstrated here offers at the very least a doubling, but even an order-of-magnitude increase in the efficiency of line surveys with ALMA on bright targets.

claims.hypothesis: High-redshift dusty star-forming galaxies host diverse ISM excitation conditions and gas inflow/outflow kinematics.
claims.experiment: Constructed CO SLEDs up to J=18 from ANGELS and BEARS data and measured velocity offsets of 12 CH+ and OH+ absorption lines across 6 galaxies relative to systemic CO.
claims.result: ~36 ± 13% of sources show elevated high-J CO SLEDs; 2 of 6 absorption-line sources show blueshifted outflows and 3 show redshifted inflows (with HerBS-21 significantly redshifted beyond error margins), with matching velocity offsets between CH+ and OH+.
claims.finding: DSFGs have diverse excitation conditions with about a third containing warm, dense gas, and show both inflows and outflows where shocked (CH+) and diffuse (OH+) gas trace similar dynamical regions.

evidence.quote: CO line transitions indicate a diverse set of excitation conditions with a fraction of the sources (∼ 35%) showcasing dense, warm gas.
Three of the sources (-21, -36 and -104) have evidence of inflowing gas in their absorption lines, although only the relative velocities of HerBS-21 are outside of the error margins.

claims.hypothesis: Resolved gas and star-formation surface densities and lensing reconstructions can distinguish whether bright Herschel DSFGs are compact starbursts or extended/merging systems.
claims.experiment: Performed uv-plane lensing reconstruction (PyAutoLens) and image-plane fitting (IMFIT) in Band 7, and compared pixel-by-pixel Band 7 continuum to low-J CO maps on the Schmidt-Kennicutt diagram.
claims.result: 9 sources are strongly lensed (mu = 2.3 to 28.3) with compact intrinsic radii (0.3-2.2 kpc), while unlensed HyLIRGs are more extended (2-12 kpc) and clumpy; pixel-by-pixel depletion times span 100 Myr to 1 Gyr with an order-of-magnitude internal spread.
claims.finding: The DSFG population is a combination of compact lensed central starbursts and extended, clumpy unlensed HyLIRGs, requiring efficient gas fueling from extended reservoirs to sustain central star formation.

evidence.quote: The resolved gas to star-formation surface densities vary strongly per source, and suggest that the observed diversity of dusty star-forming galaxies could be a combination of lensed, compact dusty starbursts and extended, potentially-merging galaxies.

evidence.loc: 6.1 The resolved star-formation law in ANGELS sources
evidence.quote: The order of magnitude spread in the pixel-per-pixel surface gas densities and surface star-formation rates indicates that DSFGs require efficient feeding of gas from the gas-rich regions into star-forming regions

why_this_data.value: Sources within 10 degrees on the sky with known spectroscopic redshifts from BEARS allow shared calibration in configurations C43-6 and lower, enabling 2-minute snapshots across Bands 3-8 to sample rest-frame 200-2000 GHz at 0.5-0.1 arcsec resolution.

evidence.quote: The number density of sources allowed the use of short snapshots (≈ 2 min) with only a single ∼ 20 - 30 min. calibration step to reduce the overheads typically associated with line surveys (∼one calibration per targeted line).
This shared calibration step is only enabled for sources within 10 deg. on the sky for configurations below ∼ 3 km (C43-6 or lower)

why_this_method.value: Tuning optimization triples targeted lines; visibility-plane two-phase lens modelling avoids parametric bias on complex resolved structures; extended continuum+moment-0 apertures recover total line flux in resolved sources.

evidence.quote: The simple act of optimizing the tuning towards the known spectroscopic redshifts can triple the number lines within any snapshot program.

Effectively, we test the best aperture for each line to include as much flux as possible, favouring larger apertures to measure the total flux as accurately as possible at the potential cost of signal-to-noise ratio.
In such cases, relying on a parametric model could introduce biases in the lens parameters and, by extension, in the derived magnification factors

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Pure 2-sigma moment-0 apertures or pure dust continuum apertures for line flux extraction, rejected in favor of a combined extended aperture to avoid false positives and missing edge flux.

evidence.quote: In an effort to extract the total line fluxes, we tried several flux measurement techniques, including 2𝜎 moment-0 apertures (biased to including false positive 2𝜎 features and missing the 0−2𝜎 regions on the edges of the contours; Stanley et al. 2023) and dust continuum apertures (presuming dust and star-formation are coincident with line emission).

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Curve-of-growth aperture stopping at 5-sigma SNR (used in BEARS), which biases resolved line fluxes slightly low compared to the ANGELS matched-aperture method.

evidence.quote: in this paper we match the apertures to extract flux despite the additional noise that arises from increased apertures, while previous studies use a curve-of-growth approach that stops velocity-integrated flux density measurements at a 5𝜎 threshold, which appears to bias the observed fluxes low.

limitations_admitted.value: Snapshot observations are inhomogeneous in line coverage per source and not deep enough to guarantee detections of all targeted lines, introducing potential detection bias.

evidence.quote: Firstly, the ANGELS method is efficient, but does not provide the homogeneity of targeted observations with ALMA. In fact, these observations are not deep enough to guarantee a detection

limitations_admitted.value: Line stacking only probes average population-wide behavior and is dominated by the brightest sources due to variance weighting.

evidence.quote: As discussed in detail by Hagimoto et al. (2023) and Reuter et al. (2023), this means that the brightest sources are still predominantly determining the spectrum.
Since DSFGs are found to be a diverse population, line stacking alone cannot reveal more than population-wide behaviour

limitations_admitted.value: Tuning optimization did not optimize the variable intermediate frequency of Band 6, did not account for lines already observed in BEARS, and did not account for smaller primary beams at higher frequencies missing wide companions.

evidence.quote: Band 6 has a variable intermediate frequency which has not been further optimized during these ANGELS observations, and would require higher-order optimization steps to fully explore.

these graphs do not account for the change in primary beam sensitivity with increasing frequency. As several of our sources were known multiples, we are unable to resolve some sources across all bands.

limitations_admitted.value: Some lines sit near the edge of spectral windows (e.g., [OI] 145 um in HerBS-41A only probes delta V < 150 km/s; [NII] in HerBS-81B only covers V > 50 km/s; CH+(2-1) in HerBS-36 may miss delta V < 0 km/s).

evidence.quote: Meanwhile, this is only the second time that CH+(2–1) is seen in the z > 0.1 Universe (Bakx et al. 2024), although we note that we might miss the ΔV < 0 km/s component in the ANGELS observations.
The [O i] emission line was detected in HerBS-41A, although we note that the total flux estimate might be underestimated since we probe only the ΔV < 150 km/s region.

limitations_admitted.value: Resolved Schmidt-Kennicutt analysis uses mid-J CO transitions (J=3-2 to 6-5) and a constant alpha_CO = 4.0, which introduces conversion uncertainties, and the >1-sigma pixel cut truncates outskirts.

evidence.loc: 6.1 The resolved star-formation law in ANGELS sources
evidence.quote: Additionally, CO line tracers between CO(3–2) and CO(6–5) are used for the molecular gas mass estimates, which add additional uncertainties in the conversion to the ground-state, i.e., to the luminosity of CO(1–0).

evidence.loc: 6.1 The resolved star-formation law in ANGELS sources
evidence.quote: Note that the sharp lines in resolved Schmidt-Kennicutt relations in Figure G2, particularly for HerBS-25 and -106, come from the > 1𝜎 criterion.

referee_caveats_inferred: Differential lensing can distort high-J CO SLEDs and line ratios since compact warm regions may be magnified differently from extended cold gas, and spectral lines were not individually lens-modeled.

Converting Band 7 continuum and mid-J CO (up to CO 6-5) pixel-by-pixel into Sigma_SFR and Sigma_H2 assuming a fixed T_d = 35 K and alpha_CO = 4.0 across all pixels ignores spatial gradients in dust temperature, optical depth, and excitation.
Several reported line detections in Table C1 have integrated flux SNR below 2-3 sigma (e.g., OH+ in HerBS-42A at -0.40 +/- 0.32 Jy km/s) or hit the upper linewidth boundary of 941 km/s.

reproducibility.score_reason: ALMA project codes, exact frequency tunings, CASA versions, weighting, deconvolver, uv-taper, pixel sizes, beam sizes, and per-line aperture thresholds (in Figure C1) are thoroughly documented; minor deductions for unstated tclean stopping thresholds, final cube channel widths, and PyAutoLens priors.
